note: Cross-repo contract for the entitlement push. This file is duplicated byte-for-byte in work-address/app and work-address/web; they are separate repositories, so each owns a copy. `revision` is monotonic per owner and the product ignores a push with a lower one than it holds; `validUntil` is when the grant lapses without further news, after which the product stops treating the account as premium. web asserts it PRODUCES these bytes and this signature; app asserts it ACCEPTS them. Changing one without the other breaks entitlement in production in a way neither suite would otherwise catch, so change both in the same pull request or not at all. ROUTE BINDING: every internal route shares one secret, so the signature names the route it was made for. `signature` is the header value, `v2=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256 with the shared secret over `signedBytes` - the version, `method`, `path`, the header name in lower case and then `serialised`, joined by single newlines - so these bytes signed for this route are refused on every other. `legacySignature` is the form used before the binding, the bare hex HMAC of `serialised` alone: app accepts it only while APP_INTERNAL_SIGNATURE_ACCEPT_LEGACY is on, web sends it only as the fallback after a 401 while APP_INTERNAL_SIGNATURE_LEGACY_FALLBACK is on, and both go when that one-release window closes (docs/internal-signature.md in each repository).
